subject: Hospitality
title: Allergy Management on the Floor
description: A micro-lesson that makes Allergy Management on the Floor usable.

hook.text: A guest with a severe peanut allergy eats a sauce containing peanut oil. Anaphylaxis follows.

buildup.text: Food allergies affect 8% of children and 5% of adults. Every table potentially has someone who could be harmed by hidden items.

discovery.text: Robust allergy management requires allergen-coded menus, trained servers, kitchen communication systems, and separate prep areas.

twist.text: The legal liability is enormous. A single allergy incident can result in wrongful death lawsuits, criminal charges.

climax.text: The best restaurants empower any staff member to stop service if an allergy concern is raised—safety overrides speed, always.

punchline.text: One missed allergen can be fatal. Allergy management is a life-or-death protocol.

quiz.question: Why is allergy management a critical protocol in restaurants?
options: Food allergies can cause anaphylaxis—legal and safety risks are enormous
